newsitem.title: USA: Dow Chemical earnings beat estimates but stock falls.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical earnings beat estimates but stock falls.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co. Thursday reported better-than-expected earnings for the fourth quarter, aided by strong sales that helped offset price declines for many of its key products.

The nation's No. 2 chemical producer said earnings fell 1.4 percent to $409 million in the quarter. But the results, equal to $1.69 a share, beat Wall Street forecasts of $1.62 a share, according to First Call, which tracks estimates.
In the 1995 quarter, Dow earned $415 million, or $1.63 a share, when there was more stock outstanding. Ongoing stock repurchases last year reduced the amount of shares.
Volume growth offset price declines and boosted sales 7 percent in the quarter to $4.90 billion from $4.59 billion.
Results for the quarter also included a pretax gain of $77 million on the sale of a stake in an oil pipeline.
Although the results beat analysts' published forecasts, Dow's stock fell 12.5 cents to close at $78.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.

The company said plastics volume jumped 17 percent while chemicals and metals volume gained 12 percent in the quarter. Agricultural chemicals did well in Latin America and Asia due to new products such as its Clincher rice herbicide, Dow said.

Prices fell in the quarter for important products such as polystyrene, a plastic used to make refrigerator linings, packaging and other items, and lye, used in paper-making and in other industries, the company said.
But volume growth, improved productivity and cost cutting largely offset lower prices and higher energy and feedstock costs.
"We have made solid progress," Dow Chemical President William Stavropoulos said. "But our drive for improved productivity will not stop."

For the year, earnings fell to $1.90 billion, or $7.71 a share, from $2.07 billion, or $7.72 a share, the company said. The 1995 results included a gain of $169 million from asset sales and a $330 million charge related to the Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing of its 50-percent owned Dow Corning Corp.
Sales edged lower to $20.05 billion from the record $20.20 billion in 1995.
Operating income for the year was $3.1 billion compared with $3.9 billion in 1995.
The company said it cut selling, administrative and research and development expenses by $98 million last year, meeting its target.
